Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, Nxeon hosting platform, admin portal at /admin). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated git worktree:
  cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-adminfreemc -b feature/admin-freemc main
Then `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-adminfreemc`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/.env .env`. Do all work there, not in /opt/nxeon directly.

CONTEXT: The free Minecraft product (one free Docker-based Minecraft server per account on a dedicated "freemc-host" VM) has NO dedicated admin-portal visibility today — admins can't see the list of free servers, their status/preset/public-listing state, or manage them, separately from the paid-VPS admin views. The user wants a proper admin section for this.

READ FIRST, in full:
- `lib/admin-groups.ts` — the admin sidebar nav config (`ADMIN_NAV`). Find the "Servers" group (has "Servers" → `/admin/servers` and "Game servers" → `/admin/games`) and add a new entry for this feature, e.g. `{ label: "Free Minecraft", href: "/admin/free-minecraft" }`, in that same group.
- `app/admin/games/page.tsx` (and/or `app/admin/servers/page.tsx`) — study the existing pattern for an admin list-of-servers page: table/grid layout, status badges, search/filter if present, admin action buttons. Match this look/pattern for the new page rather than inventing a new style.
- `prisma/schema.prisma`'s `FreeMinecraftServer` model — fields available: `id`, `userId`/`user` relation, `subdomain`, `containerName`, `status`, `name`, `preset`, `createdAt`, `isPublic`, `publicTagline`, `publicDescription`, `extraMods`.
- `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` — the customer-facing server actions (`getFreeMinecraftDashboard`, power controls, etc.) and the `freemcHost()` helper for reaching the dedicated Docker host via `withServerSsh`. You'll likely want your own small set of admin-scoped read/action functions rather than reusing the customer ones directly (those check `requireUser()` against the CALLER's own server; admin actions need to operate on ANY server by id, with an admin-role check instead).
- `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` — `FREEMC_PRESETS` (for showing a friendly preset label), `getFreeServerStatus`/`getFreeServerPlayers` (for live running/player-count status), `sendRcon`.
- Check how existing admin pages verify the caller is an admin (likely `requireAdmin()` or a role check in `lib/auth.ts` — grep for how `app/admin/games/page.tsx` or similar gates access) and use the identical pattern.

BUILD:
1. `app/admin/free-minecraft/page.tsx` — a table/list of ALL `FreeMinecraftServer` rows (paginate or cap at a sane number like 100 + note the cap, don't silently truncate without saying so), each showing: owner (user email/name), subdomain + connect address, display name, active preset (friendly label via `FREEMC_PRESETS`), status, public-listing state (badge if `isPublic`), created date. Live running/player-count status is a nice-to-have — if you include it, do NOT do it as N sequential SSH calls on page load (that would be slow/fragile for a growing list); either skip live status entirely for the list view and note that as a deliberate choice, or fetch it lazily/client-side per-row on demand (e.g. a "check status" button per row) rather than blocking the page.
2. A simple summary/stats header: total free servers, how many are `READY` vs other statuses, how many are public.
3. Basic admin actions — at minimum, the ability to delete a stray/abandoned server (SSH `docker rm -f` + `rm -rf` its data dir, same pattern as the customer-facing `deleteFreeMinecraftServer` in `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`, but admin-gated and operating on any server by id) and to force `isPublic` off (a moderation lever — e.g. if a public listing needs to be pulled). Put these in a new `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts`, `"use server"`, with an admin-role check at the top of every exported function (never trust the UI alone).
4. Wire the nav entry into `lib/admin-groups.ts` as described above.
5. A per-server detail view is optional/nice-to-have if you have time (e.g. `app/admin/free-minecraft/[id]/page.tsx` showing more detail + console access) — the list page with basic moderation actions is the must-have, don't over-scope at the expense of shipping the core page cleanly.

Do NOT edit `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`, `components/customer/freemc/*`, or `prisma/schema.prisma` — this is a new, separate admin surface reading the same data, not a change to the customer-facing feature.

`npx tsc --noEmit` and a full `npm run build` must both pass clean before you finish. Commit your work explicitly (named files, never `-A`). Do not merge to main or push. Do not delete your worktree — I'll integrate it.

Report back: the file paths created, what admin actions you implemented, your decision on live-status-in-list-view, and confirmation build/typecheck passed.

/**
 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
 *
 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav

export type Area =
  | "overview"
  | "analytics"
  | "clients"
  | "support"
  | "fleet"
  | "billing"
  | "platform";

/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  platform: ["ADMIN"],
};

export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);

Committed on branch `feature/admin-freemc` at `/opt/nxeon-wt-adminfreemc`. Not merged to main, not pushed, worktree left in place as instructed.

## Summary

**Files created/modified** (all under `/opt/nxeon-wt-adminfreemc`):

- `app/admin/free-minecraft/page.tsx` — new admin list page.
- `components/admin/FreeMinecraftControls.tsx` — client components for the row actions.
- `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts` — new `"use server"` admin actions file.
- `lib/admin-groups.ts` — added `{ label: "Free Minecraft", href: "/admin/free-minecraft" }` to the existing "Servers" entry's tab list (alongside Servers / Grant VPS / Game servers).
- `lib/rbac.ts` — added `"/admin/free-minecraft": "fleet"` to `HREF_AREA`, matching the sibling `/admin/servers` mapping (ADMIN-only, same as the page's own `requireArea("fleet")` guard).

**Page contents**: summary header (total servers, READY count, public count via `StatCard`), then a table capped at 100 rows (explicit "showing the 100 most recent of N" note if exceeded — no silent truncation) showing owner, display name, connect address (`subdomain.<free_minecraft_domain>`), preset (friendly label from `FREEMC_PRESETS`), status (`StatusDot`), public/private (`Badge`), created date, and per-row actions. Matches the existing `app/admin/games/page.tsx` / `app/admin/servers/page.tsx` visual pattern (`PageHeader`, `StatCard`, `Badge`, `StatusDot`, `EmptyState`, `table-shell`).

**Admin actions implemented** (`lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts`, each independently gated with `requireArea("fleet")`, looked up by row `id` rather than caller):
- `adminGetFreeMinecraftStatus(id)` — on-demand live running/player-count check.
- `adminUnpublishFreeMinecraftServer(id)` — moderation lever, forces `isPublic` off, audit-logged.
- `adminDeleteFreeMinecraftServer(id)` — `docker rm -f` + `rm -rf` data dir on freemc-host (same shape as the customer-facing delete), then deletes the DB row regardless of SSH outcome; audit-logged.

**Live-status decision**: deliberately *not* fetched for the whole list on page load — that would be N sequential SSH calls to freemc-host and would get slower/more fragile as the list grows. Instead each row has a "Check status" button (`CheckStatusButton` in `FreeMinecraftControls.tsx`) that does one SSH round trip only when clicked. This is called out explicitly in an on-page note, not left unexplained.

**Not built**: the optional per-server detail view (`[id]/page.tsx`) — skipped in favor of shipping the list page cleanly, per the instructions' priority.

**Guardrails respected**: did not touch `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`, `components/customer/freemc/*`, or `prisma/schema.prisma`. Worktree's symlinked `node_modules` was never staged (`git add` used explicit file paths, not `-A`).
